hunks.baseline: An unidentified Supreme Peak master whose name and identity were unknown.
hunks.sol: An unidentified Supreme Peak master. No one knew his name or anything about him.

hunks.baseline: My first impression of the extraordinary man who, about a dozen years ago, subdued Ningxia Province—then little better than a lawless wasteland—in a single stroke, only to defy everyone’s expectations and retire into a life of idleness, was this:
hunks.sol: About a dozen years ago, he had subdued the lawless Ningxia Province in a single stroke, then defied everyone’s expectations by settling into a life of idleness. My first impression of this extraordinary man was:

hunks.baseline: *He looks like a damn beggar.*
hunks.sol: *He looks like a beggar.*

hunks.baseline: His hair and beard were long enough to cover his face and reach his waist, and so matted they looked like one solid mass.
hunks.sol: His hair and beard were so long they covered his face and reached his waist. Worse, they were matted together.

hunks.baseline: His clothes were torn and stained in so many places that “rags” would have been the more accurate description. And the stench coming off his grime-caked body was so revolutionary it was practically an evolution of its own.
hunks.sol: His clothes were torn and stained in so many places that “rags” would have been more accurate. And the stench coming off his grime-caked body was innovative—no, revolutionary.

hunks.baseline: A wretch. A king of beggars.
hunks.sol: An utter pauper. The king of beggars.

hunks.baseline: I’d spent enough time rolling around in Gates to have built up some resistance, which was the only reason I could stand there. Even now, the stench was bad enough to make me wonder if it could really be coming from a human body.
hunks.sol: I’d spent enough time rolling around in Gates to be able to stand there and take it. Even now, the stench was bad enough to make me wonder if it could really be coming from a human body.

hunks.baseline: I desperately breathed through my mouth to block out as much of the smell as possible, then tried to push the man away. But his legs were planted deep in the ground like thousand-pound boulders. He didn’t budge.
hunks.sol: I desperately breathed through my mouth to block out as much of the smell as possible, then tried to push the man away. But his legs were planted deep in the ground like a thousand-pound boulder. He didn’t budge.

hunks.baseline: *Looking at that, he really does seem like a Great Sir…*
hunks.sol: *Looking at that, he really does seem to be the Great Sir…*

hunks.baseline: It was like hearing that Kim, the homeless guy who ran the second exit at Seoul Station, had turned out to be the chairman of a major corporation.
hunks.sol: It was like finding out that Kim, the homeless guy who ruled the second exit at Seoul Station, was actually the chairman of a major corporation.

hunks.baseline: *But, seriously, why are you crying so hard?*
hunks.sol: *But seriously, why are you crying so hard?*

hunks.baseline: As I stood there, unsure what to do and darting my eyes around, the strange man—no, the Great Sir—who’d been wailing in my arms finally spoke in a congested voice.
hunks.sol: As I stood there, unsure what to do and darting my eyes around, the strange man—no, the Great Sir—who’d been wailing in my arms finally spoke in a stuffy voice.

hunks.baseline: “Ahem. Ahem. Sorry about that. It was such a moving moment that the tears came before I knew it.”
hunks.sol: “Ahem. Ahem. Forgive me. It was such a moving moment that I couldn’t help crying.”

hunks.baseline: “I don’t think tears were the only thing that came out.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t think tears were the only thing coming out.”

hunks.baseline: I could understand tears and a runny nose, but why he had to let them both out while clinging to me was beyond me. Still, I nodded, summoning the bare minimum of patience and respect for my elder.
hunks.sol: Tears and snot, fine, but why did he have to get them all over me? Still, I nodded, summoning the bare minimum of patience and respect for my elder.

hunks.baseline: “You really do everything, don’t you?”
hunks.sol: “You’ve got to be kidding me.”

hunks.baseline: The Great Sir thanked me in a guileless voice, then blew his nose with a sound that seemed to clear out his entire head.
hunks.sol: The Great Sir thanked me in a guileless voice, then blew his nose with a sound that suggested he’d cleared out everything inside him.

hunks.baseline: On my clothes.
hunks.sol: Into the hem of my clothes.

hunks.baseline: To sum it up, even with half my sanity gone, I somehow managed not to punch the Great Sir in the head.
hunks.sol: To sum it up, even with half my self-control gone, I somehow managed not to punch the Great Sir in the face.

hunks.baseline: Starting a fight in the middle of a battlefield that hadn’t even been fully secured yet would have been unwise. More than that, Perfected Being Hyeoncheon had quickly grasped what was happening and stepped in.
hunks.sol: Starting a fight in the middle of a battlefield that hadn’t been fully secured yet would have been unwise. More than that, Perfected Being Hyeoncheon had quickly grasped what was happening and stepped in.

hunks.baseline: It was a sight that would have surprised anyone. No—astonished them.
hunks.sol: Anyone would have found the sight surprising. No, astonishing.

hunks.baseline: The Sect Leader of the Kongtong Sect, one of the Nine Sects and One Gang; a hero of the Great Faction War; and a Supreme Peak master representing Gansu Province.
hunks.sol: The Sect Leader of the Kongtong Sect, one of the Nine Sects and One Gang; a hero of the Great Faction War; and a Supreme Peak master representing Gansu.

hunks.baseline: If we were talking about the Marine Corps, he’d be a legendary first-wave veteran who’d taken part in the Incheon Landing Operation. He had the seniority to stand in the middle of the world and shout, “Everyone below me and above you, fall in!”
hunks.sol: In Marine Corps terms, he was a legendary first-class veteran who’d even fought in the Incheon Landing Operation. He had the seniority to stand in the middle of the world and shout, “Everyone below me and above you, fall in!”

hunks.baseline: And yet this man, whose standing in the Murim and martial prowess both ranked among the highest in the world, was the first to offer a fist-and-palm salute with the utmost respect.
hunks.sol: And yet this man, whose standing in Murim and martial prowess both ranked among the highest in the world, was the first to offer a fist-and-palm salute with the utmost respect.

hunks.baseline: Maybe the filthy-looking fellow had a video file with a title like *Kongtong’s Perfected One H and His Secret Hand Games*.
hunks.sol: Maybe the filthy-looking fellow had a video file titled something like *Kongtong’s Perfected One H and His Secret Hand Games*.

hunks.baseline: But there was a reason everyone could understand why Perfected Being Hyeoncheon would show that much respect to a strange man followed by little more than some former mounted bandits.
hunks.sol: But there was a reason anyone could understand why Perfected Being Hyeoncheon would show such respect to a strange man followed by a bunch of former mounted bandits.

hunks.baseline: To sum up the story, it went like this.
hunks.sol: The story went like this.

hunks.baseline: At the time, Perfected Being Hyeoncheon and the Kongtong Sect survivors had been defeated at Dunhuang and had no idea where to go.
hunks.sol: After their defeat at Dunhuang, Perfected Being Hyeoncheon and the Kongtong Sect survivors had no idea where to go.

hunks.baseline: They had to flee east to avoid Dark Heaven’s forces gathering like clouds in the west. But now that they felt betrayed by their allies, heading east would have been like walking straight into a tiger’s jaws.
hunks.sol: They needed to flee east, away from Dark Heaven’s forces gathering like clouds in the west. But with suspicion of their allies already taking root, heading east felt like walking straight into a tiger’s jaws.

hunks.baseline: “We considered turning south for Qinghai, but we had no idea what Dark Heaven might already have done there. We had no choice but to head for the grasslands, where fewer people lived.”
hunks.sol: “We considered turning south for Qinghai, but we had no idea what Dark Heaven might already have done there. We had no choice but to head for the grasslands, where far fewer people lived.”

hunks.baseline: Though Qinghai lay at the far edge of the Central Plains, it was still watched from every direction.
hunks.sol: Though Qinghai lay at the far edge of the Central Plains, there were still plenty of eyes watching from every direction.

hunks.baseline: The grasslands, by contrast, were vast and sparsely populated, which made them better for evading pursuit. If Dark Heaven had reached both places, anyone would have chosen the latter.
hunks.sol: The grasslands, by contrast, were vast and sparsely populated, making them better for evading pursuit. If Dark Heaven had reached both places, anyone would have chosen the latter.

hunks.baseline: “We kept heading north without rest. Even after passing Anxi and entering the grasslands, we couldn’t let our guard down. We considered taking a short break to recover and see what was happening in Gansu, or perhaps crossing the grasslands and going all the way to Shaanxi.”
hunks.sol: “We kept heading north without rest. Even after passing Anxi and entering the grasslands, we couldn’t let our guard down. We thought we might pause long enough to recover, then see what was happening in Gansu. Or perhaps cross the grasslands and go all the way to Shaanxi.”

hunks.baseline: But for the Kongtong Disciples, already suffering injuries both serious and minor from the fierce battle at Dunhuang, it was an exhausting march.
hunks.sol: But for the Kongtong Disciples, already suffering injuries both serious and minor from the fierce battle at Dunhuang, it was a grueling march.

hunks.baseline: Even Perfected Being Hyeoncheon, who had to lead them all, had reached his limit from severe internal injuries.
hunks.sol: Even Perfected Being Hyeoncheon, who had to lead them all, had reached his limit from a severe Internal Injury.

hunks.baseline: “Still, we couldn’t stop. We had no choice but to keep moving, feeling helpless and miserable. Then, after several days on the road, one night we saw a light flickering in the distance.”
hunks.sol: “Still, we couldn’t stop. Miserable and unsure what lay ahead, we had no choice but to keep moving. Then, after several days on the road, we saw a light flickering in the distance one night.”

hunks.baseline: For the fugitives crossing that endless expanse, any light in the dark was something to be wary of.
hunks.sol: For the fugitives crossing that endless expanse, any light in the dark was cause for alarm.

hunks.baseline: “We crept closer, holding our breath. There was some strange man roasting camel meat. It had been four days since we’d seen food, and we were all half out of our minds.”
hunks.sol: “We crept closer, keeping as quiet as we could. A strange man was roasting camel meat. It was the first food we’d seen in four days, and we were all half out of our minds.”

hunks.baseline: “Indeed. He saw us shivering in the cold and invited us over without hesitation.”
hunks.sol: “Indeed. He saw us shivering in the cold and invited us to sit with him without hesitation.”

hunks.baseline: “As soon as he saw us, he devoured all the meat before our eyes and told us we could warm ourselves by the fire for a while, then go our separate ways.”
hunks.sol: “As soon as he saw us, he wolfed down all the meat and told us we could warm ourselves by the fire for a while before we went our separate ways.”

hunks.baseline: “Regardless, the Great Sir helped us greatly. He gave me and all the Disciples of our sect a place to hide for a while and treated the wounded.”
hunks.sol: “Regardless, the Great Sir helped us greatly. He gave every Disciple of our sect, myself included, a place to hide for a while and treated the wounded.”

hunks.baseline: It was said that a master could recognize a master.
hunks.sol: A master could recognize another master.

hunks.baseline: “Oh, I must have mixed that up. The Black-Horse Seven?”
hunks.sol: “Oh, I must have mixed that up. The Seven Masters of Black Horse?”

hunks.baseline: Quite a few mounted figures were riding among the battlefield, their horses snorting roughly.
hunks.sol: Quite a few riders were moving across the battlefield on snorting horses.

hunks.baseline: They wore relatively light leather armor and carried weapons like spears and crescent-bladed polearms. Now I could finally be sure who they were.
hunks.sol: They wore relatively light leather armor and carried weapons such as lances and crescent-bladed polearms. Now I could finally be sure who they were.

hunks.baseline: The Seven Masters of Baekma Bang had promised a few days ago that they would bring the Great Sir back. They’d returned with the horse caravans under their command, and thanks to them, we’d been able to deal a decisive, fatal blow to the enemies who were on the verge of collapse.
hunks.sol: The Seven Masters of Baekma Bang had promised a few days ago that they would bring the Great Sir back. They’d returned with the horse caravans under their command, and thanks to them, we’d been able to deal a decisive blow to the collapsing enemy forces.

hunks.baseline: But they had kept the promise they made to me, even if they were a little later than they’d planned. And with the Great Sir’s kindness, Perfected Being Hyeoncheon and the Kongtong Disciples had recovered from their injuries and returned to Gansu alongside thousands of horse-caravan riders.
hunks.sol: But they had kept the promise they made to me, even if they were a little later than planned. And with the Great Sir’s help, Perfected Being Hyeoncheon and the Kongtong Disciples had recovered from their injuries and returned to Gansu alongside thousands of horse-caravan riders.

hunks.baseline: Still, there was one question I couldn’t answer.
hunks.sol: Still, one question remained.

hunks.baseline: A moment ago, he’d clung to me and sobbed as if we were reuniting with a long-lost family. Now he was yawning widely just because the story had gotten a little long. As expected, he seemed far from sane.
hunks.sol: A moment ago, he’d clung to me and sobbed as if we were long-lost family reunited. Now he was yawning openly just because the story had gotten a little long. He certainly didn’t seem quite sane.

hunks.baseline: And I quietly, secretly reached out toward the Great Sir.
hunks.sol: Quietly, secretly, I reached out toward the Great Sir.

hunks.baseline: A hand of detection, invisible and permitted only to me.
hunks.sol: With a hand of detection, invisible and granted to me alone.

hunks.baseline: *Skill: Activate Qi Sense.*
hunks.sol: *Skill, activate Qi Sense.*

hunks.baseline: The blue circle spread outward from me, at last reaching the Great Sir.
hunks.sol: The blue circle spread outward from me and finally reached the Great Sir.
